#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))

- **PR #**: 1723

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T14:18:30Z

## PR Description

Closes #1722
### Root Cause

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1723._

> ℹ️ **4 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` line 135

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the new `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture is inert — `seq -f` always errors, so the stub can never model a running job and the transient test passes vacuously**

`seq -f` requires the format to contain a `%` directive; `'{"status":"in_progress"}'` has none, so GNU seq (and BSD seq) exits 1 on every call:

```bash
$ seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 2
seq: format ‘{"status":"in_progress"}’ has no % directive   # exit 1
```

The stub swallows that failure (`2>/dev/null || true`), so `body` is **always empty** and every `--json jobs` poll answers `{"jobs":[]}` → the script's running-job count is **always 0**, regardless of the fixture value. Verified empirically against the stub's exact pipeline, and confirmed behaviorally:

1. The documented contract at line 70 — "absent file = 1 job always running (healthy child) so older fixtures without job modeling keep their behavior" — is **false**: an absent file yields `n=1`, but the count still comes out 0.
2. The `0\n1\n` fixture in the transient test never registers a running job: poll 2's `1` is silently ignored.
3. Consequence: the guard's **positive path (`last_running="$now"` on a running job) has zero effective coverage in the whole suite**. I disabled that line (`last_running="$now"` → no-op) and re-ran the transient test — it **still passes** ("a transient between-jobs pickup gap does not trip the guard" is green with a deliberately broken guard), because three fast polls finish well inside the 2s stall window and the fixture never reports a running job either way.

The main queue-stall test passes for the right reason only because it wants `0`; everything that depends on modeling "a job IS running" is dead. The next change to the refresh logic would land with a fully green suite.

Suggested fix (no `seq -f` needed):

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
```

(n=0 → empty body → `{"jobs":[]}` ✓, n≥1 → comma-joined objects ✓.)

Then make the transient test actually exercise the refresh: e.g. have the stub log the served count (see suggestion on line 120) or assert on the gh log that a poll with a running job preceded the completion, so a broken `last_running` refresh turns the test red.

---

### Thread 2 — `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` line 87

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the 600s stall window cannot distinguish a zombie-held pool from a legitimately busy one — concurrent legs will false-wedge healthy queued children**

The guard treats "not completed + no job `in_progress` for 600s" as the zombie signature, but on this repo's concurrent leg design the same signature is produced by a **healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job** on the shared single-runner macOS pool:

- All dispatching legs are `needs: plan` siblings (daily-publish.yml) — testflight and cli dispatch within seconds of each other.
- testflight's `build-ios`/`submit-ios` are pinned to the ONE runner (`runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]`); cli's `build-macos` matrix (arm64/x86_64, `timeout-minutes: 150` each) runs on `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the same pool.
- If cli's matrix leg #1 lands on fa-m5-1 first, the testflight child shows "version done, nothing in_progress" for up to ~300m. The new guard cancels that healthy child at 600s, re-dispatches into the same occupied pool, and at ~20m into attempt 2 fails the leg and cancels the re-dispatch — a red leg with a misleading "runner pool suspect" diagnostic, where the pre-PR watcher would have waited within its 250m budget and gone green on any pool that freed within ~30m. Hosted-runner (ubuntu-latest) queue crunches can produce the same false wedge for the play/website/addin children.

Note the arithmetic headroom is generous: the second-wedge fail-fast fits every leg's ceiling even with a much larger window (e.g. 30m: 2×(~10m version + 30m stall) + 13m cancel ≈ 93m ≪ 150m addin ceiling). Please either (a) raise `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` default into that range, (b) scale it off the leg budget (`max(600, budget/8)`), or (c) document this accepted false-wedge class in the script header — today the comment "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" is only true for the first (hosted) job of the chain, not for the self-hosted jobs that queue behind sibling legs.

---

### Thread 3 — `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: one `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call instead of two**

The watch loop now makes two sequential `gh run view` calls per poll (status+conclusion, then jobs). They can be merged into a single call:

```bash
read -r status running < <(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
  --jq '"\(.status)", ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null) || true
```

Benefits: halves the API traffic per poll (the poll runs every 60s for hours), and removes the benign race window between the two calls (status says `in_progress`, the run completes, the jobs call then reports 0 and ticks the stall clock for one iteration — harmless at a 600s threshold today, but one call makes it structurally impossible).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))

  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20): the re-dispatched testflight
  # child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker (a job-level
  # timeout is enforced BY the runner, so a hung worker outlives its own
  # 90m ceiling and never processes the run cancel either) — the leg burned
  # its remaining ~107m watching a child that could never start and died as
  # a bare 360m ceiling kill. The watcher now also treats "not completed
  # but NO job in_progress for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600s)" as a wedge
  # riding the same one self-heal, and cancels the child on the fail path
  # so an orphaned queued run can't publish unattended when the pool
  # revives. Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg

    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')

    steps:

          # slow TestFlight

          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \

- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` line 135

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the new `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture is inert — `seq -f` always errors, so the stub can never model a running job and the transient test passes vacuously**

`seq -f` requires the format to contain a `%` directive; `'{"status":"in_progress"}'` has none, so GNU seq (and BSD seq) exits 1 on every call:

```bash
$ seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 2
seq: format ‘{"status":"in_progress"}’ has no % directive   # exit 1
```

The stub swallows that failure (`2>/dev/null || true`), so `body` is **always empty** and every `--json jobs` poll answers `{"jobs":[]}` → the script's running-job count is **always 0**, regardless of the fixture value. Verified empirically against the stub's exact pipeline, and confirmed behaviorally:

1. The documented contract at line 70 — "absent file = 1 job always running (healthy child) so older fixtures without job modeling keep their behavior" — is **false**: an absent file yields `n=1`, but the count still comes out 0.
2. The `0\n1\n` fixture in the transient test never registers a running job: poll 2's `1` is silently ignored.
3. Consequence: the guard's **positive path (`last_running="$now"` on a running job) has zero effective coverage in the whole suite**. I disabled that line (`last_running="$now"` → no-op) and re-ran the transient test — it **still passes** ("a transient between-jobs pickup gap does not trip the guard" is green with a deliberately broken guard), because three fast polls finish well inside the 2s stall window and the fixture never reports a running job either way.

The main queue-stall test passes for the right reason only because it wants `0`; everything that depends on modeling "a job IS running" is dead. The next change to the refresh logic would land with a fully green suite.

Suggested fix (no `seq -f` needed):

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
```

(n=0 → empty body → `{"jobs":[]}` ✓, n≥1 → comma-joined objects ✓.)

The new guard cancels that healthy child at 600s, re-dispatches into the same occupied pool, and at ~20m into attempt 2 fails the leg and cancels the re-dispatch — a red leg with a misleading "runner pool suspect" diagnostic, where the pre-PR watcher would have waited within its 250m budget and gone green on any pool that freed within ~30m. Hosted-runner (ubuntu-latest) queue crunches can produce the same false wedge for the play/website/addin children.

Note the arithmetic headroom is generous: the second-wedge fail-fast fits every leg's ceiling even with a much larger window (e.g. 30m: 2×(~10m version + 30m stall) + 13m cancel ≈ 93m ≪ 150m addin ceiling). The watch loop now makes two sequential `gh run view` calls per poll (status+conclusion, then jobs). They can be merged into a single call:

```bash
read -r status running < <(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
  --jq '"\(.status)", ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null) || true
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")

    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then

        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"

## PR Description

Closes #1722
### Root Cause

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi

## PR Description

Closes #1722
### Root Cause

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

### Fix

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh`: added a job-level liveness guard — a not-completed run with **no job in `in_progress` for `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` (600s)** is a wedge and rides the existing one-shot self-heal (cancel + re-dispatch once, then fail fast naming the pool). The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` line 135

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the new `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture is inert — `seq -f` always errors, so the stub can never model a running job and the transient test passes vacuously**

`seq -f` requires the format to contain a `%` directive; `'{"status":"in_progress"}'` has none, so GNU seq (and BSD seq) exits 1 on every call:

```bash
$ seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 2
seq: format ‘{"status":"in_progress"}’ has no % directive   # exit 1
```

The stub swallows that failure (`2>/dev/null || true`), so `body` is **always empty** and every `--json jobs` poll answers `{"jobs":[]}` → the script's running-job count is **always 0**, regardless of the fixture value. Verified empirically against the stub's exact pipeline, and confirmed behaviorally:

1. The documented contract at line 70 — "absent file = 1 job always running (healthy child) so older fixtures without job modeling keep their behavior" — is **false**: an absent file yields `n=1`, but the count still comes out 0.
2. The `0\n1\n` fixture in the transient test never registers a running job: poll 2's `1` is silently ignored.
3. Consequence: the guard's **positive path (`last_running="$now"` on a running job) has zero effective coverage in the whole suite**. I disabled that line (`last_running="$now"` → no-op) and re-ran the transient test — it **still passes** ("a transient between-jobs pickup gap does not trip the guard" is green with a deliberately broken guard), because three fast polls finish well inside the 2s stall window and the fixture never reports a running job either way.

The main queue-stall test passes for the right reason only because it wants `0`; everything that depends on modeling "a job IS running" is dead. The next change to the refresh logic would land with a fully green suite.

Suggested fix (no `seq -f` needed):

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
```

(n=0 → empty body → `{"jobs":[]}` ✓, n≥1 → comma-joined objects ✓.)

Then make the transient test actually exercise the refresh: e.g. have the stub log the served count (see suggestion on line 120) or assert on the gh log that a poll with a running job preceded the completion, so a broken `last_running` refresh turns the test red.

The new guard cancels that healthy child at 600s, re-dispatches into the same occupied pool, and at ~20m into attempt 2 fails the leg and cancels the re-dispatch — a red leg with a misleading "runner pool suspect" diagnostic, where the pre-PR watcher would have waited within its 250m budget and gone green on any pool that freed within ~30m. Hosted-runner (ubuntu-latest) queue crunches can produce the same false wedge for the play/website/addin children.

Note the arithmetic headroom is generous: the second-wedge fail-fast fits every leg's ceiling even with a much larger window (e.g. 30m: 2×(~10m version + 30m stall) + 13m cancel ≈ 93m ≪ 150m addin ceiling). Please either (a) raise `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` default into that range, (b) scale it off the leg budget (`max(600, budget/8)`), or (c) document this accepted false-wedge class in the script header — today the comment "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" is only true for the first (hosted) job of the chain, not for the self-hosted jobs that queue behind sibling legs.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: one `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call instead of two**

The watch loop now makes two sequential `gh run view` calls per poll (status+conclusion, then jobs). They can be merged into a single call:

```bash
read -r status running < <(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
  --jq '"\(.status)", ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null) || true
```

Benefits: halves the API traffic per poll (the poll runs every 60s for hours), and removes the benign race window between the two calls (status says `in_progress`, the run completes, the jobs call then reports 0 and ticks the stall clock for one iteration — harmless at a 600s threshold today, but one call makes it structurally impossible).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done

The 2026-10-20 `Leg: TestFlight` watcher was killed at its 360m ceiling with no diagnostics while the re-dispatched child run ([39402285750](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/39402285750)) sat `queued` forever: the hung self-hosted worker ignored its own 90m job ceiling (250m actual), never processed the watcher's `gh run cancel` either, and kept holding the single-runner pool. `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` polls **run** status only — it saw `in_progress` throughout, burned the remaining ~107m of leg time on a child that could never start, and died as a bare timeout (hence "no failed-step log available"), leaving the orphan queued to publish unattended on pool revival.

The watcher now also cancels the child on the fail path so a server-side-dead run can never publish unattended when the pool revives. A second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg (testflight ≈ 273m < 360m ceiling).
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml`: arithmetic comment updated (gh-172 case).
- Ops: cancelled the orphaned queued run `39402285750` (the containment the fixed watcher performs).

### Test Coverage

- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — `gh-172` group: pool-held child (alive, nothing running) stalls into the one self-heal, fails fast with the pool signature on attempt 2, cancels the orphan; plus a transient between-jobs pickup gap that must NOT trip the guard. New stub fixture (`jobs-<id>.txt`) models `gh run view --json jobs`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — **11376 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Notes

- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table is untouched.
- The physical `fa-m5-1` worker itself needs ops attention (reboot/de-register); the guard only bounds the leg damage and makes the signature visible in the leg log.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1723._

> ℹ️ **4 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` line 135

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the new `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture is inert — `seq -f` always errors, so the stub can never model a running job and the transient test passes vacuously**

`seq -f` requires the format to contain a `%` directive; `'{"status":"in_progress"}'` has none, so GNU seq (and BSD seq) exits 1 on every call:

```bash
$ seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 2
seq: format ‘{"status":"in_progress"}’ has no % directive   # exit 1
```

The stub swallows that failure (`2>/dev/null || true`), so `body` is **always empty** and every `--json jobs` poll answers `{"jobs":[]}` → the script's running-job count is **always 0**, regardless of the fixture value. Verified empirically against the stub's exact pipeline, and confirmed behaviorally:

1. The documented contract at line 70 — "absent file = 1 job always running (healthy child) so older fixtures without job modeling keep their behavior" — is **false**: an absent file yields `n=1`, but the count still comes out 0.
2. The `0\n1\n` fixture in the transient test never registers a running job: poll 2's `1` is silently ignored.
3. Consequence: the guard's **positive path (`last_running="$now"` on a running job) has zero effective coverage in the whole suite**. I disabled that line (`last_running="$now"` → no-op) and re-ran the transient test — it **still passes** ("a transient between-jobs pickup gap does not trip the guard" is green with a deliberately broken guard), because three fast polls finish well inside the 2s stall window and the fixture never reports a running job either way.

The main queue-stall test passes for the right reason only because it wants `0`; everything that depends on modeling "a job IS running" is dead. The next change to the refresh logic would land with a fully green suite.

Suggested fix (no `seq -f` needed):

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
```

(n=0 → empty body → `{"jobs":[]}` ✓, n≥1 → comma-joined objects ✓.)

Then make the transient test actually exercise the refresh: e.g. have the stub log the served count (see suggestion on line 120) or assert on the gh log that a poll with a running job preceded the completion, so a broken `last_running` refresh turns the test red.

---

### Thread 2 — `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` line 87

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the 600s stall window cannot distinguish a zombie-held pool from a legitimately busy one — concurrent legs will false-wedge healthy queued children**

The guard treats "not completed + no job `in_progress` for 600s" as the zombie signature, but on this repo's concurrent leg design the same signature is produced by a **healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job** on the shared single-runner macOS pool:

- All dispatching legs are `needs: plan` siblings (daily-publish.yml) — testflight and cli dispatch within seconds of each other.
- testflight's `build-ios`/`submit-ios` are pinned to the ONE runner (`runs-on: [self-hosted, macos-m5, fa-m5-1]`); cli's `build-macos` matrix (arm64/x86_64, `timeout-minutes: 150` each) runs on `[self-hosted, macos-m5]` — the same pool.
- If cli's matrix leg #1 lands on fa-m5-1 first, the testflight child shows "version done, nothing in_progress" for up to ~300m. The new guard cancels that healthy child at 600s, re-dispatches into the same occupied pool, and at ~20m into attempt 2 fails the leg and cancels the re-dispatch — a red leg with a misleading "runner pool suspect" diagnostic, where the pre-PR watcher would have waited within its 250m budget and gone green on any pool that freed within ~30m. Hosted-runner (ubuntu-latest) queue crunches can produce the same false wedge for the play/website/addin children.

Note the arithmetic headroom is generous: the second-wedge fail-fast fits every leg's ceiling even with a much larger window (e.g. 30m: 2×(~10m version + 30m stall) + 13m cancel ≈ 93m ≪ 150m addin ceiling). Please either (a) raise `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` default into that range, (b) scale it off the leg budget (`max(600, budget/8)`), or (c) document this accepted false-wedge class in the script header — today the comment "A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" is only true for the first (hosted) job of the chain, not for the self-hosted jobs that queue behind sibling legs.

---

### Thread 3 — `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` line 144

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: one `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call instead of two**

The watch loop now makes two sequential `gh run view` calls per poll (status+conclusion, then jobs). They can be merged into a single call:

```bash
read -r status running < <(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
  --jq '"\(.status)", ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null) || true
```

Benefits: halves the API traffic per poll (the poll runs every 60s for hours), and removes the benign race window between the two calls (status says `in_progress`, the run completes, the jobs call then reports 0 and ticks the stall clock for one iteration — harmless at a 600s threshold today, but one call makes it structurally impossible).

---

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.

arguments.newText:
view)
        id="\$3"
        # gh-172 review: the watcher polls with ONE
        # `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; the stub
        # serves that merged shape from BOTH fixture families:
        #  view-<id>.txt — one `<status> <conclusion>` line per poll,
        #                  last line repeats once exhausted;
        #  jobs-<id>.txt — one running-job COUNT per poll, last line
        #                  repeats; ABSENT file = 1 job always running
        #                  (healthy child) so older fixtures without job
        #                  modeling keep their behavior. cancelled = 0.
        # Every served count is appended to served-jobs-<id>.log so tests
        # can prove the fixture actually modeled a running job. The
        # gh-172 review BLOCKING bug: `seq -f '{"status":...}'` has no %
        # directive, so seq ALWAYS errored, the swallowed failure left
        # body empty and every poll answered {"jobs":[]} — the fixture
        # was inert and the refresh path had zero coverage.
        is_jobs=0
        for ((j = 0; j < \${#args[@]} - 1; j++)); do
          if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ]; then
            case "\${args[\$((j + 1))]}" in
              *jobs*) is_jobs=1 ;;
            esac
          fi
        done
        if [ "\$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
          if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
            printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled","jobs":[]}' | apply_jq
          else
            vf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$vf" ]; then
              line=\$(head -1 "\$vf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$vf" && rm -f "\$vf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$vf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$vf"; fi
              status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
            else
              status=unknown; conclusion=-
            fi
            jf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$jf" ]; then
              n=\$(head -1 "\$jf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$jf" && rm -f "\$jf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi
            else
              n=1
            fi
            printf '%s\\n' "\$n" >> "\$GH_STUB_DIR/served-jobs-\$id.log"
            # n=0 → empty body → {"jobs":[]} ✓; n≥1 → comma-joined
            # objects ✓ (no `seq -f` — its format needs a % directive).
            body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
            printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s","jobs":[%s]}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" "\$body" | apply_jq
          fi
        elif [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
          printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled"}' | apply_jq
        else
          f="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
          line=\$(head -1 "\$f")
          sed -i.bak '1d' "\$f" && rm -f "\$f.bak"
          if ! [ -s "\$f" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$f"; fi
          status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
          printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" | apply_jq
        fi
        ;;

### Thread 1 — `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` line 135

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-20):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the new `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture is inert — `seq -f` always errors, so the stub can never model a running job and the transient test passes vacuously**

`seq -f` requires the format to contain a `%` directive; `'{"status":"in_progress"}'` has none, so GNU seq (and BSD seq) exits 1 on every call:

```bash
$ seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 2
seq: format ‘{"status":"in_progress"}’ has no % directive   # exit 1
```

The stub swallows that failure (`2>/dev/null || true`), so `body` is **always empty** and every `--json jobs` poll answers `{"jobs":[]}` → the script's running-job count is **always 0**, regardless of the fixture value. Verified empirically against the stub's exact pipeline, and confirmed behaviorally:

1. The documented contract at line 70 — "absent file = 1 job always running (healthy child) so older fixtures without job modeling keep their behavior" — is **false**: an absent file yields `n=1`, but the count still comes out 0.
2. The `0\n1\n` fixture in the transient test never registers a running job: poll 2's `1` is silently ignored.
3. Consequence: the guard's **positive path (`last_running="$now"` on a running job) has zero effective coverage in the whole suite**. I disabled that line (`last_running="$now"` → no-op) and re-ran the transient test — it **still passes** ("a transient between-jobs pickup gap does not trip the guard" is green with a deliberately broken guard), because three fast polls finish well inside the 2s stall window and the fixture never reports a running job either way.

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)

The watch loop now makes two sequential `gh run view` calls per poll (status+conclusion, then jobs). They can be merged into a single call:

read -r status running < <(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
