#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))

  # 90m ceiling and never processes the run cancel either) — the leg burned

{"newText":"cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done

```bash
$ seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 2
seq: format ‘{"status":"in_progress"}’ has no % directive   # exit 1
```

The stub swallows that failure (`2>/dev/null || true`), so `body` is **always empty** and every `--json jobs` poll answers `{"jobs":[]}` → the script's running-job count is **always 0**, regardless of the fixture value. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))

  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20): the re-dispatched testflight
  # child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker (a job-level
  # timeout is enforced BY the runner, so a hung worker outlives its own
  # 90m ceiling and never processes the run cancel either) — the leg burned
  # its remaining ~107m watching a child that could never start and died as
  # a bare 360m ceiling kill. The watcher now also treats "not completed
  # but NO job in_progress for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600s)" as a wedge
  # riding the same one self-heal, and cancels the child on the fail path
  # so an orphaned queued run can't publish unattended when the pool
  # revives. Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg

    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.

            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \

{"newText":"cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
# legitimate waits.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi

# Test shim (dispatch_watch_test.dart): print the effective knobs and exit
# without dispatching anything.
if [ "${DW_DUMP_KNOBS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "budget=$budget queue_stall=$queue_stall poll=$poll cancel_wait=$cancel_wait"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and watch it — with correct run correlation
# (issue #343) and wedge self-healing (issue #344). Shared by every
# dispatching daily-publish leg so the nightly legs cannot regress to the
# old inline watchers.
#
# #343 — the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch the SAME workflow
# (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan` siblings; the old inline
# watcher identified "our" run by event + a 60s createdAt window only and
# grabbed [0] of the timestamp-ordered list, so the Play leg could latch
# the TestFlight run (or a stale same-shaped run inside the trailing
# window) and watch a build that never builds Android. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago, like today's stale iOS failure, is out of scope).
#
# #344 — a self-hosted runner that lost its final job-completion report
# holds a SUCCEEDED job in_progress forever (GitHub has no stale-run
# detection for self-hosted jobs below the workflow timeout), blocking the
# single-runner pool and every watcher leg until their 300m timeout. The
# watch here is budgeted: a run still unfinished after --budget-seconds
# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way.
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600 — gh-172:
# no-running-job wedge window).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
budget=$((2 * 60 * 60))
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --budget-seconds) budget="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--budget-seconds N] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# A healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds; the signature
# means the run is waiting on a pool that will never free — the 2026-10-20
# TestFlight leg (run 39374894901) burned ~107m of leg time watching a
# re-dispatched child queued forever on a zombie self-hosted worker and then
# died as a bare 360m ceiling kill with no diagnostic.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-600}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

attempt=1
while :; do
  dispatch
  epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the #34 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    running=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs \
      --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length' 2>/dev/null) || running=""
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ $((now - last_running)) -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    elif [ $((now - started)) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done

    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.

Now I understand the codebase. Let me plan the fixes for the three threads:

### Thread 1 (BLOCKING) — `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart:135`
The stub's `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "$n" 2>/dev/null || true` always errors because the format has no `%` directive. So `body` is always empty and the jobs count is always 0.

Fix: use `body=$(seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)`.

Also, make the transient test actually exercise the refresh: assert on the gh log that a poll with a running job preceded the completion, so a broken `last_running` refresh turns the test red.

Let me think about how the transient test works:
- `view-111.txt`: `in_progress -\nin_progress -\ncompleted success\n` — 3 polls: in_progress, in_progress, completed success.
- `jobs-111.txt`: `0\n1\n` — poll 1: 0 running, poll 2: 1 running, then repeats 1.
- `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=2`.

    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.

    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null

        #                  modeling keep their behavior. cancelled = 0.

        # body empty and every poll answered {"jobs":[]} — the fixture
        # was inert and the refresh path had zero coverage.
        is_jobs=0
        for ((j = 0; j < \${#args[@]} - 1; j++)); do
          if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ]; then
            case "\${args[\$((j + 1))]}" in
              *jobs*) is_jobs=1 ;;
            esac
          fi
        done
        if [ "\$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
          if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
            printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled","jobs":[]}' | apply_jq
          else
            vf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$vf" ]; then
              line=\$(head -1 "\$vf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$vf" && rm -f "\$vf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$vf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$vf"; fi
              status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
            else
              status=unknown; conclusion=-
            fi
            jf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$jf" ]; then
              n=\$(head -1 "\$jf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$jf" && rm -f "\$jf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi

            body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)

The stub's `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "$n" 2>/dev/null || true` always errors because the format has no `%` directive. So `body` is always empty and the jobs count is always 0.

Fix: use `body=$(seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)`.

Also, make the transient test actually exercise the refresh: assert on the gh log that a poll with a running job preceded the completion, so a broken `last_running` refresh turns the test red.

Let me think about how the transient test works:
- `view-111.txt`: `in_progress -\nin_progress -\ncompleted success\n` — 3 polls: in_progress, in_progress, completed success.
- `jobs-111.txt`: `0\n1\n` — poll 1: 0 running, poll 2: 1 running, then repeats 1.
- `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=2`.

For a broken refresh (`last_running="$now"` disabled), `last_running` stays at start time. With poll interval 0 (DW_POLL_SECONDS=0), three fast polls finish well inside 2s. So even with fixture `0\n0\n` (always 0 running), the test would pass since elapsed < 2s stall window.

Hmm, wait. For the transient test to actually exercise the refresh path, the poll timing must be such that without the `last_running` refresh, the stall window WOULD be exceeded. That's tricky with a 0 poll interval and fast polls.

The reviewer suggested: "make the transient test actually exercise the refresh: e.g. have the stub log the served count (see suggestion on line 120) or assert on the gh log that a poll with a running job preceded the completion, so a broken `last_running` refresh turns the test red."

Hmm, "so a broken `last_running` refresh turns the test red" — but merely asserting on the log that a poll reported a running job doesn't directly verify the `last_running` refresh. It verifies the fixture is no longer inert — that the positive path was hit at least once. That is the *minimal* requirement: with the inert fixture, the refresh line NEVER executes with running > 0. Asserting the log contains a jobs poll whose response had a running job ensures the fixture works. But to verify the refresh itself works, we'd need to observe the `last_running` variable... which is internal to the script.

Actually, a cleaner behavioral approach: make the transient test such that a broken refresh (no update of `last_running`) would cause the guard to trip and cancel the child, turning the test red. How? The guard trips when `now - last_running > queue_stall`. With a broken refresh, `last_running = started`. The guard trips when `now - started > queue_stall`. So if the transient test has a stall window (e.g. DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=2) and the transient gap lasts longer than the window... wait, no. Let me think.

Sequence for a healthy transient:
- Poll 1: 0 running (gap starts). last_running = start (set at loop start before polling).
- Poll 2: 1 running → refresh last_running = now.
- Poll 3: completed → break.

With broken refresh, last_running stays at start. The guard trips if `now - last_running > stall_window` on a poll where running == 0. Poll 1 has running == 0, so `now - last_running` ≈ 0 (just started). Poll 2 has running == 1, guard not evaluated for stall. Poll 3 completes.

So the transient case passes vacuously with a broken refresh because poll 1 happens immediately after start. To make a broken refresh fail, we'd need a second 0-running poll AFTER the stall window has elapsed since the last 0-running poll... but with a refresh, that second gap must still be shorter than the window relative to the refreshed timestamp.

Design: 
- Poll 1: 0 running at t=0 (last_running=start=t0).
- Sleep ~2.5s... but wait, polls use DW_POLL_SECONDS. We set DW_POLL_SECONDS to sleep between polls. Hmm, but the timing is `now - last_running > queue_stall`.

Let me design with real timing:
- DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS = 2, DW_POLL_SECONDS = 1.
- Poll 1 (t≈0): 0 running. now - last_running ≈ 0 < 2 → no trip.
- Sleep 1s.
- Poll 2 (t≈1): 1 running → last_running = now (t≈1). [broken refresh: stays t≈0]
- Sleep 1s.
- Poll 3 (t≈2): 0 running. now - last_running ≈ 1 < 2 → no trip. [broken: now - last_running ≈ 2 → not > 2... borderline!]
- Sleep 1s.
- Poll 4 (t≈3): completed → break. Hmm, poll 4's status check happens first; completed breaks before the guard.

Borderline is flaky. Let me use a bigger margin:
- DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS = 1, DW_POLL_SECONDS = 1.
- Poll 1 (t≈0): 0 running. 0 < 1 → no trip.
- Poll 2 (t≈1): 1 running → last_running = t≈1. [broken: t≈0]
- Poll 3 (t≈2): 0 running. now - last_running ≈ 1 → NOT > 1 → no trip (borderline again).

Timing is inherently racy with 1s granularity. Not great.

Alternative approach the reviewer suggested: assert on the gh log that a poll with a running job preceded the completion. This ensures the fixture is actually serving a running job at some point (i.e., the positive path of the guard IS exercised — `last_running="$now"` executes with a real running count). But can we *verify* the refresh happened? 

Actually we can combine: have the stub log the served count. Then the test asserts: (a) at least one poll served count ≥ 1 (fixture not inert — RED with the broken `seq -f` because all served counts are 0), and (b) the run completed successfully without cancellation. 

Does a broken `last_running` refresh turn this red? Only if timing makes the guard trip without refresh. As computed, with a broken refresh the guard trips when `now - started > stall` on a 0-running poll. To make that deterministic-ish in a fast test, we can't easily.

Hmm wait — actually, there IS a deterministic way to test the refresh path without wall-clock racing: the "stall clock" `last_running` is reset on running > 0. Consider the main queue-stall test: attempts with `jobs=0` forever. It trips after queue_stall seconds. What if we craft a test where:
- The child starts with a running job for a while (last_running refreshed),
- then goes to 0,
- and the guard should trip relative to when the running job ended, not when the run started.

With a broken refresh, the guard would trip EARLIER (relative to start). With correct refresh, it trips later. To distinguish deterministically we need timing separation: stall window W, running job until t1, then 0-running. Correct guard trips at t1 + W + ε. Broken guard trips at t0 + W + ε where t0 < t1.

Deterministic test design using poll counts and sleeps:

- Poll 2 (t≈1): 1 running → last_running = t≈1. (broken: t0)

Ugh, borderline at the boundary because `>` is strict. Need `now - last_running > W` to be clearly true/false. With 1s polls and W=2, values pass through 1, 2, 3. Value 2 is borderline (depends on sub-second jitter). 

OK let me use larger margins: W = 3, poll = 2s.
- Poll 1 (t≈0): 1 running → last_running ≈ 0.
- Poll 2 (t≈2): 1 running → last_running ≈ 2.
- Poll 3 (t≈4): 0 running → correct: 4-2=2 < 3 → no trip. broken: 4-0=4 > 3 → TRIP (cancels the healthy child → test goes red with exit 1).
- Poll 4 (t≈6): completed success → break, exit 0.

Correct guard: exit 0, one dispatch.   #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)

  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20): the re-dispatched testflight
  # child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker (a job-level
  # timeout is enforced BY the runner, so a hung worker outlives its own
  # 90m ceiling and never processes the run cancel either) — the leg burned
  # its remaining ~107m watching a child that could never start and died as
  # a bare 360m ceiling kill. The watcher now also treats "not completed
  # but NO job in_progress for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600s)" as a wedge
  # riding the same one self-heal, and cancels the child on the fail path
  # so an orphaned queued run can't publish unattended when the pool
  # revives. Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg
  # (testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 10m stall = 273m < 360m).

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |

    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.

        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null

  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)

  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20): the re-dispatched testflight
  # child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker (a job-level
  # timeout is enforced BY the runner, so a hung worker outlives its own
  # 90m ceiling and never processes the run cancel either) — the leg burned
  # its remaining ~107m watching a child that could never start and died as
  # a bare 360m ceiling kill. The watcher now also treats "not completed
  # but NO job in_progress for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600s)" as a wedge
  # riding the same one self-heal, and cancels the child on the fail path
  # so an orphaned queued run can't publish unattended when the pool
  # revives. Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg
  # (testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 10m stall = 273m < 360m).

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a

          # Budget 250m = child worst-case 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351; gh-1477 moved the version ceiling
          # 10 → 20m — blobless fetch + seatbelt) + 20m margin — a healthy

          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m

          rc=0

  #   play       version 20 → build-android 45 →              95m   →  110m (6600s) ; 240m
  #             submit-android 30 (∥ release-mobile 15)
  #   cli        version 20 → build-macos 150×2 (arm64 +      335m  →  350m (21000s) ; 360m
  #             x86_64 SERIALIZE on the single self-hosted
  #             runner) → release-macos 15
  #             (∥ cli matrix 45, extension 30 — shorter paths)
  #   (gh-1477: the version/plan jobs' ceiling moved 10 → 20m — a
  #   full-history fetch outgrew the 10m bomb; the fetch is now blobless
  #   and 20m is the seatbelt. Worst-cases and budgets grew by exactly
  #   the +10m.)
  #   website    pages build 45 → deploy 15                   60m   →   75m (4500s)  ; 180m
  #   addin      office-addin-suite 45 (single job)           45m   →   60m (3600s)  ; 150m
  #
  # Second-wedge headroom (2×budget + ~15m vs leg timeout): play 235 ≤
  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (515 > 360)
  # and cli (715 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.
  #
  # gh-172 (run 39374894901, 2026-10-20): the re-dispatched testflight
  # child sat queued FOREVER on the zombie self-hosted worker (a job-level
  # timeout is enforced BY the runner, so a hung worker outlives its own
  # 90m ceiling and never processes the run cancel either) — the leg burned
  # its remaining ~107m watching a child that could never start and died as
  # a bare 360m ceiling kill. The watcher now also treats "not completed
  # but NO job in_progress for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (600s)" as a wedge
  # riding the same one self-heal, and cancels the child on the fail path
  # so an orphaned queued run can't publish unattended when the pool
  # revives. Second wedge now ends in a diagnostic inside the leg
  # (testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 10m stall = 273m < 360m).

    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 230m (version 20 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 250m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (515m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'

          exit 1

{"newText":"  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # ONE gh call per poll (gh-172 review): status/conclusion and the
    # in_progress job count come from the same snapshot — half the API
    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.
    status=""
    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
    ) || true
    if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the gh-172 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    # The #34 budget check sits OUTSIDE the refresh branch below: the
    # original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held in_progress forever) shows
    # running>0 on every poll and only ever trips the budget — chaining the
    # budget behind the refresh would disarm it exactly when a job is
    # (nominally) running.
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$((now - last_running))" -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$wedge" ] && [ "$((now - started))" -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi

{"newText":"      view)
        id="\$3"
        # gh-172 review: the watcher polls with ONE
        # `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; the stub
        # serves that merged shape from BOTH fixture families:
        #  view-<id>.txt — one `<status> <conclusion>` line per poll,
        #                  last line repeats once exhausted;
        #  jobs-<id>.txt — one running-job COUNT per poll, last line
        #                  repeats; ABSENT file = 1 job always running
        #                  (healthy child) so older fixtures without job
        #                  modeling keep their behavior. cancelled = 0.
        # Every served count is appended to served-jobs-<id>.log so tests
        # can prove the fixture actually modeled a running job. The
        # gh-172 review BLOCKING bug: `seq -f '{"status":...}'` has no %
        # directive, so seq ALWAYS errored, the swallowed failure left
        # body empty and every poll answered {"jobs":[]} — the fixture
        # was inert and the refresh path had zero coverage.
        is_jobs=0
        for ((j = 0; j < \${#args[@]} - 1; j++)); do
          if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ]; then
            case "\${args[\$((j + 1))]}" in
              *jobs*) is_jobs=1 ;;
            esac
          fi
        done
        if [ "\$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
          if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
            printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled","jobs":[]}' | apply_jq
          else
            vf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$vf" ]; then
              line=\$(head -1 "\$vf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$vf" && rm -f "\$vf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$vf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$vf"; fi
              status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
            else
              status=unknown; conclusion=-
            fi
            jf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$jf" ]; then
              n=\$(head -1 "\$jf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$jf" && rm -f "\$jf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi
            else
              n=1
            fi
            printf '%s\\n' "\$n" >> "\$GH_STUB_DIR/served-jobs-\$id.log"
            # n=0 → empty body → {"jobs":[]} ✓; n≥1 → comma-joined
            # objects ✓ (no `seq -f` — its format needs a % directive).
            body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
            printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s","jobs":[%s]}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" "\$body" | apply_jq
          fi
        elif [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
          printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled"}' | apply_jq
        else
          f="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
          line=\$(head -1 "\$f")
          sed -i.bak '1d' "\$f" && rm -f "\$f.bak"
          if ! [ -s "\$f" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$f"; fi
          status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
          printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" | apply_jq
        fi
        ;;","oldText":"      view)
        id="\$3"
        # `--json jobs` polls (gh-172 queue-stall guard) are served from
        # jobs-<id>.txt: one running-job COUNT per poll, last line repeats;
        # absent file = 1 job running (healthy child) so older fixtures
        # without job modeling keep their behavior. cancelled = 0.
        is_jobs=0
        for ((j = 0; j < \${#args[@]} - 1; j++)); do
          if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ] && [ "\${args[\$((j + 1))]}" = "jobs" ]; then is_jobs=1; fi
        done
        if [ "\$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
          if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
            n=0
          else
            jf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$jf" ]; then
              n=\$(head -1 "\$jf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$jf" && rm -f "\$jf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi
            else
              n=1
            fi
          fi
          body=\$(seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "\$n" 2>/dev/null || true)
          printf '{"jobs":[%s]}' "\$body" | apply_jq
        elif [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
          printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled"}' | apply_jq
        else
          f="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
          line=\$(head -1 "\$f")
          sed -i.bak '1d' "\$f" && rm -f "\$f.bak"
          if ! [ -s "\$f" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$f"; fi
          status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
          printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" | apply_jq
        fi
        ;;","path":"test/dispatch_watch_test.dart"}

{"newText":"cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
# legitimate waits.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi

# Test shim (dispatch_watch_test.dart): print the effective knobs and exit
# without dispatching anything.
if [ "${DW_DUMP_KNOBS:-0}" = "1" ]; then

  - `DW_POLL_SECONDS: '2'` (env), `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS: '3'`, budget 30 (so budget can't fire first).
  - Timeline: poll 1 (t≈0): jobs=1 → refresh; poll 2 (t≈2): jobs=1 → refresh; poll 3 (t≈4): jobs=0 → correct: 4-2=2 ≤ 3 no trip; poll 4 (t≈6): completed success → exit 0.

Poll 1 t≈0: 0-0=0 ≤ 3; poll 2 t≈2: 2 ≤ 3 no; poll 3 t≈4: 4 > 3 → WEDGE → cancel + re-dispatch → runs.json still only 111 (no runs2.json) → latch 111 → cancelled marker → completed/canceled → exit 1. Poll 3: running=0 → stall: 2 > 3 false → budget elif: 4 - 0 = 4 > 30? no → no wedge. Poll 4: completed → break → exit 0 GREEN. Hmm — so the transient test alone doesn't force the guard restructure. Right: the guard restructure is forced by the OTHER new test (budget-while-running) and by the #34 tests with the honest fixture (they'd hang). Wait — no!   'double-wedge': same hang → RED.
   
  So fixing the stub FIRST turns the #34 tests red (by hang), demonstrating the elif-chain bug the honest fixture exposes. Then the guard restructure turns them green. That's the TDD sequence:
   
  - RED-1: add redesigned transient + absent-contract + knobs tests → run → RED (transient fails on inert fixture; absent-contract test fails; knobs fails).
  - GREEN-1a: fix stub body construction (seq|sed|paste) + served log + merged-call serving. But the stub serving change must match the script's call shape... The script change (merged call) and the stub serving change must land together or tests break: if I fix ONLY the body construction (keeping `--json jobs` adjacent detection), the script still makes two calls → stub works as before for separate jobs polls → #34 tests hang (running=1 always → refresh → budget dead). So GREEN-1a alone = hang on #34. I should do stub fix + guard restructure + merged call in one GREEN step (they're one coherent fix), after demonstrating RED. The TDD rule says: test must fail before the fix — it will (I'll run RED first). Fine to fix script+stub in one GREEN step.

2. **Absent-file contract + budget-while-running test** (`an absent jobs fixture means a healthy running child — the budget self-heal, not the stall guard`):

  - Honest stub: running=1 every poll → stall never (refresh); budget fires at >2s → attempt 1 'still unfinished after 2s' → cancel + re-dispatch → attempt 2 same → fail fast → exit 1.
  - Assertions: exit 1; 2 dispatches; out contains 'still unfinished'; out does NOT contain 'no running job'; cancel 111 + cancel 222 in log.
  - Pre-fix (inert stub): running=0 → stall wedge at 1s fires FIRST → 'no running job' appears → assertion `isFalse(contains('no running job'))` fails → RED (fast, no hang) ✓.
  - Post stub-fix, pre guard-restructure: HANG (30s timeout) → also RED (uglier but still red). Either way RED before fix. 

3. **Default-window scaling test** (Thread 2): with new `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` shim:
  ```dart
  test('stall window defaults to max(600, budget/8) — scaled off the leg budget', () {
    // budget 800s → window 100s
    final dw1 = runDw('knobs-scaled', ['pages.yml'], {'runs.json': '[]'}, env: {'DW_DUMP_KNOBS': '1', '--budget...'});

Assert log contains 'queue_stall=100'. And with default budget (720): queue_stall=900. And floor: budget 800 → 100; budget 100 → 125 < 600? No: 100/8=125 <600 → floor 600. Test: budget 800 → 100 (above floor), budget 800... wait 800/8=100 <600 → floor → 600! Oops. budget/8 > 600 requires budget > 480. So: budget 800 → 100 (scaled, > floor); budget 800 → 600 (floor). Assert both.
  - Pre-fix: no DW_DUMP_KNOBS → script runs the dispatch flow: runs.json '[]' → wait_for_run exhausts 20 attempts × 0s → 'never appeared' → exit 1, no 'queue_stall=' line → RED ✓ (fast).
  - Post-fix: prints knobs, exit 0 → GREEN.
   
  Where does the output go? `echo` → stdout → dw.out. Assert `dw.out` contains 'queue_stall=100' etc. But also the log would have the invocation line. Fine, assert on dw.out.

  Note: with DW_DUMP_KNOBS=1, the script must exit BEFORE dispatching. Place the shim right after knob computation (before the jq selector? After — the selector needs title; put the shim after `queue_stall` computation and before `title_select`... title_select computation is harmless. Put shim right after the knobs block).

Simpler: assert `dw.log.any((l) => l.contains('--json status,conclusion,jobs'))` — pins the merged call shape. And the transient served-count assertion pins fixture honesty. Also maybe assert no separate `--json jobs` (exactly-adjacent) call remains in the hot loop... The cancel-wait still uses `--json status` — fine. {"newText":"      view)
        id="\$3"
        # gh-172 review: the watcher polls with ONE
        # `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call; the stub
        # serves that merged shape from BOTH fixture families:
        #  view-<id>.txt — one `<status> <conclusion>` line per poll,
        #                  last line repeats once exhausted;
        #  jobs-<id>.txt — one running-job COUNT per poll, last line
        #                  repeats; ABSENT file = 1 job always running
        #                  (healthy child) so older fixtures without job
        #                  modeling keep their behavior. cancelled = 0.
        # Every served count is appended to served-jobs-<id>.log so tests
        # can prove the fixture actually modeled a running job. The
        # gh-172 review BLOCKING bug: `seq -f '{"status":...}'` has no %
        # directive, so seq ALWAYS errored, the swallowed failure left
        # body empty and every poll answered {"jobs":[]} — the fixture
        # was inert and the refresh path had zero coverage.
        is_jobs=0
        for ((j = 0; j < \${#args[@]} - 1; j++)); do
          if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ]; then
            case "\${args[\$((j + 1))]}" in
              *jobs*) is_jobs=1 ;;
            esac
          fi
        done
        if [ "\$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
          if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
            printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled","jobs":[]}' | apply_jq
          else
            vf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$vf" ]; then
              line=\$(head -1 "\$vf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$vf" && rm -f "\$vf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$vf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$vf"; fi
              status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
            else
              status=unknown; conclusion=-
            fi
            jf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$jf" ]; then
              n=\$(head -1 "\$jf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$jf" && rm -f "\$jf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi
            else
              n=1
            fi
            printf '%s\\n' "\$n" >> "\$GH_STUB_DIR/served-jobs-\$id.log"
            # n=0 → empty body → {"jobs":[]} ✓; n≥1 → comma-joined
            # objects ✓ (no `seq -f` — its format needs a % directive).
            body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
            printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s","jobs":[%s]}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" "\$body" | apply_jq
          fi
        elif [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
          printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled"}' | apply_jq
        else
          f="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
          line=\$(head -1 "\$f")
          sed -i.bak '1d' "\$f" && rm -f "\$f.bak"
          if ! [ -s "\$f" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$f"; fi
          status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
          printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" | apply_jq
        fi
        ;;","oldText":"      view)
        id="\$3"
        # `--json jobs` polls (gh-172 queue-stall guard) are served from
        # jobs-<id>.txt: one running-job COUNT per poll, last line repeats;
        # absent file = 1 job running (healthy child) so older fixtures
        # without job modeling keep their behavior. cancelled = 0.
        is_jobs=0
        for ((j = 0; j < \${#args[@]} - 1; j++)); do
          if [ "\${args[\$j]}" = "--json" ] && [ "\${args[\$((j + 1))]}" = "jobs" ]; then is_jobs=1; fi
        done
        if [ "\$is_jobs" = "1" ]; then
          if [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
            n=0
          else
            jf="\$GH_STUB_DIR/jobs-\$id.txt"
            if [ -f "\$jf" ]; then
              n=\$(head -1 "\$jf")
              sed -i.bak '1d' "\$jf" && rm -f "\$jf.bak"
              if ! [ -s "\$jf" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$n" > "\$jf"; fi
            else
              n=1
            fi
          fi
          body=\$(seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}' -s ',' 1 "\$n" 2>/dev/null || true)
          printf '{"jobs":[%s]}' "\$body" | apply_jq
        elif [ -f "\$GH_STUB_DIR/cancelled-\$id" ]; then
          printf '{"status":"completed","conclusion":"cancelled"}' | apply_jq
        else
          f="\$GH_STUB_DIR/view-\$id.txt"
          line=\$(head -1 "\$f")
          sed -i.bak '1d' "\$f" && rm -f "\$f.bak"
          if ! [ -s "\$f" ]; then printf '%s\\n' "\$line" > "\$f"; fi
          status="\${line%% *}"; conclusion="\${line#* }"
          printf '{"status":"%s","conclusion":"%s"}' "\$status" "\$conclusion" | apply_jq

        ;;","path":"test/dispatch_watch_test.dart"}

{"newText":"  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # ONE gh call per poll (gh-172 review): status/conclusion and the
    # in_progress job count come from the same snapshot — half the API
    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.
    status=""
    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
    ) || true
    if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the gh-172 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    # The #34 budget check sits OUTSIDE the refresh branch below: the
    # original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held in_progress forever) shows
    # running>0 on every poll and only ever trips the budget — chaining the
    # budget behind the refresh would disarm it exactly when a job is
    # (nominally) running.
    wedge=""

      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$((now - last_running))" -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$wedge" ] && [ "$((now - started))" -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
