Root cause confirmed exactly as reported: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so GNU/BSD `seq` exited 1 on every call, the swallowed failure left `body` empty, and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — the running-job count was always 0 regardless of the fixture.

**Stub fix** (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart, `stubGh`) — no `seq -f`, as suggested:

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
```

`n=0` → empty body → `{"jobs":[]}`; `n≥1` → comma-joined objects. The documented contract "absent file = 1 job always running" is now true (verified by a new test) instead of false.

**The stub now also logs every served count** to `served-jobs-<id>.log`, and the transient test asserts a running job was actually served before the gap — an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.

- `last_running="$now"` disabled (the exact experiment from the comment): the guard trips at poll 3 the same way → exit 1 (verified — the test previously stayed green with the refresh disabled, it now fails).

{"content":"# gh-1722 rework — review threads addressed (3/3)

## Issues/Notes

- CI: no failed checks on the rework head (per `ci_failures.md`); no owned violations to fix.

## Approach

**1. BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart)**

Confirmed: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so `seq` exited 1 on every call; the stub swallowed the failure and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — running-job count always 0, the "absent file = 1 job running" contract false, the refresh path untested.

- The stub logs every served count to `served-jobs-<id>.log`; tests assert a running job was actually served, so an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.
- The transient-gap test was rebuilt to exercise the refresh with real timing (`DW_POLL_SECONDS=2`, `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3`): polls 1–2 report a running job, poll 3 reports a 2s-old gap (inside the window), poll 4 completes. - Making the fixture honest exposed a second defect the old `elif` chain hid: the **#34 budget** self-heal was chained behind the stall-clock refresh, so a run with a job `in_progress` (the original #34 zombie signature) could never trip the budget. The budget check now sits outside the refresh branch, pinned by a new test (`an absent jobs fixture = healthy running child: the #34 budget self-heal fires, never the stall guard`).

```bash
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))

read -r status running < <(
  gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \

blocks.text:
epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # ONE gh call per poll (gh-172 review): status/conclusion and the
    # in_progress job count come from the same snapshot — half the API
    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.
    status=""
    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
    ) || true
    if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the gh-172 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    # The #34 budget check sits OUTSIDE the refresh branch below: the
    # original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held in_progress forever) shows
    # running>0 on every poll and only ever trips the budget — chaining the
    # budget behind the refresh would disarm it exactly when a job is
    # (nominally) running.
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$((now - last_running))" -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$wedge" ] && [ "$((now - started))" -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way, and
# the child is cancelled on the fail path so an orphaned queued run can
# never publish unattended when the pool revives. gh-172 review: the
# window is NOT a fixed 600s — it defaults to max(600, budget/8) because
# a healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the shared
# single-runner pool shows the same "nothing running" signature for hours
# (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on the one fa-m5-1 runner).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172 no-running-job wedge window, scaled off the
# leg budget so a busy shared pool is not mistaken for a zombie; gh-172
===

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
# legitimate waits.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi

# Test shim (dispatch_watch_test.dart): print the effective knobs and exit
# without dispatching anything.
if [ "${DW_DUMP_KNOBS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "budget=$budget queue_stall=$queue_stall poll=$poll cancel_wait=$cancel_wait"
  exit 0
fi

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING — fixed: the `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture is no longer inert, and the transient test now actually exercises the refresh**

Root cause confirmed exactly as reported: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so GNU/BSD `seq` exited 1 on every call, the swallowed failure left `body` empty, and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — the running-job count was always 0 regardless of the fixture.

**Stub fix** (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart, `stubGh`) — no `seq -f`, as suggested:

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
```

`n=0` → empty body → `{"jobs":[]}`; `n≥1` → comma-joined objects. The documented contract "absent file = 1 job always running" is now true (verified by a new test) instead of false.

**The stub now also logs every served count** to `served-jobs-<id>.log`, and the transient test asserts a running job was actually served before the gap — an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.

**Transient test rebuilt to exercise the refresh** (`a transient between-jobs pickup gap does not trip the guard`): it now runs with `DW_POLL_SECONDS=2` / `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3` — polls 1–2 report a running job (refresh), poll 3 reports the between-jobs gap only 2s old (inside the window), poll 4 completes. Both regressions from the finding now turn it RED:

- inert fixture (all polls serve 0): poll 3 trips the guard at 4s since start > 3s window → cancels the healthy child → exit 1 (reproduced in the RED run);
- `last_running="$now"` disabled (the exact experiment from the comment): the guard trips at poll 3 the same way → exit 1 (verified — the test previously stayed green with the refresh disabled, it now fails).

The queue-stall test additionally asserts the poll carries `--json status,conclusion,jobs` (see the merged-call thread) so the served count and status come from one snapshot.

Note: making the fixture honest exposed that the old `elif` chain also disarmed the **#34 budget** self-heal whenever a job was running (the budget was chained behind the refresh). The budget check now sits outside the refresh branch, pinned by a new test (`an absent jobs fixture = healthy running child: the #34 budget self-heal fires, never the stall guard`) — the original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held `in_progress` forever) only ever trips the budget.

{"content":"# gh-1722 rework — review threads addressed (3/3)

## Issues/Notes

- CI: no failed checks on the rework head (per `ci_failures.md`); no owned violations to fix.
- Three open review threads addressed: 1 BLOCKING (inert test stub fixture), 1 IMPORTANT (fixed 600s stall window false-wedges busy-pool children), 1 SUGGESTION (merge the two per-poll `gh run view` calls).
- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table and every `--budget-seconds`/`timeout-minutes` pair are untouched; only the stall **window** policy changed.

## Approach

**1. BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart)**

Confirmed: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so `seq` exited 1 on every call; the stub swallowed the failure and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — running-job count always 0, the "absent file = 1 job running" contract false, the refresh path untested.

- Stub body now built without `seq -f`:
  ```bash
  body=$(seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
  ```
  (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`, `n≥1` → comma-joined objects). The absent-file contract is now real and pinned by a test.
- The stub logs every served count to `served-jobs-<id>.log`; tests assert a running job was actually served, so an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.
- The transient-gap test was rebuilt to exercise the refresh with real timing (`DW_POLL_SECONDS=2`, `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3`): polls 1–2 report a running job, poll 3 reports a 2s-old gap (inside the window), poll 4 completes. Both regressions from the finding now turn it RED — verified in the RED run (inert fixture → healthy child cancelled) and by re-running the reviewer's own experiment (refresh line disabled → test fails; it previously stayed green).
- Making the fixture honest exposed a second defect the old `elif` chain hid: the **#34 budget** self-heal was chained behind the stall-clock refresh, so a run with a job `in_progress` (the original #34 zombie signature) could never trip the budget. The budget check now sits outside the refresh branch, pinned by a new test (`an absent jobs fixture = healthy running child: the #34 budget self-heal fires, never the stall guard`).

**2. IMPORTANT — fixed 600s stall window vs legitimately busy pools (scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh)**

The window now scales off the leg budget (options b+c from the thread):

```bash
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi
```

- Effective windows: testflight ~31m, cli ~44m, play ~14m, website/addin 600s floor.
- The misleading "a healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the contention reality (cli's build-macos matrix serializes on fa-m5-1 and can hold the "nothing running" signature for hours), and the residual accepted class (contention outliving the window but not the budget) is documented in the script header.
- Second-wedge arithmetic still fits every leg ceiling: worst relative case addin ≈ 46m ≪ 150m; testflight ≈ 250m + 13m cancel + 31m stall ≈ 294m < 360m (daily-publish.yml comment updated).
- Pinned by a new test asserting both the scaled branch (budget 8000s → 1000s) and the floor (budget 800s → 600s) via a `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim.

**3. SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` call per poll (scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh)**

The two sequential calls are merged into one snapshot call:

```bash
read -r status running < <(
  gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
    --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
) || true
if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
```

Half the API traffic per poll, and the between-call race (a run completing between the two calls ticks the stall clock for one iteration) is structurally impossible. API errors still degrade to progress on both clocks. The stub serves the merged shape (status/conclusion + jobs from paired fixtures per poll), and the queue-stall test asserts the merged invocation appears in the `gh` log.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — merged single-call polling; budget check decoupled from the stall-clock refresh; `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` default scaled to `max(600, budget/8)`; `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim; header/knob comments rewritten.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — stub body construction fixed (`seq | sed | paste`), merged-shape serving, `served-jobs-<id>.log` fixture-honesty log; transient-gap test rebuilt with real timing; two new tests (absent-fixture/budget-while-running, scaled default window); merged-call assertion in the queue-stall test.
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — gh-172 arithmetic comment updated for the scaled window (testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m ≈ 294m < 360m); no behavioral change.

## Test Coverage

- TDD: all four touched/red tests failed against the pre-fix watcher (RED run reproduced: inert fixture cancels the healthy transient child; stall guard fires on a running child; no scaled default; no merged call), then went GREEN after the fix; the reviewer's vacuity experiment (`last_running="$now"` disabled) now fails the transient test instead of passing.

blocks.text:
epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # ONE gh call per poll (gh-172 review): status/conclusion and the
    # in_progress job count come from the same snapshot — half the API
    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.
    status=""
    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
    ) || true
    if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the gh-172 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    # The #34 budget check sits OUTSIDE the refresh branch below: the
    # original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held in_progress forever) shows
    # running>0 on every poll and only ever trips the budget — chaining the
    # budget behind the refresh would disarm it exactly when a job is
    # (nominally) running.
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$((now - last_running))" -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$wedge" ] && [ "$((now - started))" -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way, and
# the child is cancelled on the fail path so an orphaned queued run can
# never publish unattended when the pool revives. gh-172 review: the
# window is NOT a fixed 600s — it defaults to max(600, budget/8) because
# a healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the shared
# single-runner pool shows the same "nothing running" signature for hours
# (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on the one fa-m5-1 runner).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172 no-running-job wedge window, scaled off the
# leg budget so a busy shared pool is not mistaken for a zombie; gh-172
===

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
# legitimate waits.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi

# Test shim (dispatch_watch_test.dart): print the effective knobs and exit
# without dispatching anything.
if [ "${DW_DUMP_KNOBS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "budget=$budget queue_stall=$queue_stall poll=$poll cancel_wait=$cancel_wait"
  exit 0
fi

blocks.text:
epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # ONE gh call per poll (gh-172 review): status/conclusion and the
    # in_progress job count come from the same snapshot — half the API
    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.
    status=""
    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
    ) || true
    if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the gh-172 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    # The #34 budget check sits OUTSIDE the refresh branch below: the
    # original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held in_progress forever) shows
    # running>0 on every poll and only ever trips the budget — chaining the
    # budget behind the refresh would disarm it exactly when a job is
    # (nominally) running.
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$((now - last_running))" -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$wedge" ] && [ "$((now - started))" -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way, and
# the child is cancelled on the fail path so an orphaned queued run can
# never publish unattended when the pool revives. gh-172 review: the
# window is NOT a fixed 600s — it defaults to max(600, budget/8) because
# a healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the shared
# single-runner pool shows the same "nothing running" signature for hours
# (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on the one fa-m5-1 runner).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172 no-running-job wedge window, scaled off the
# leg budget so a busy shared pool is not mistaken for a zombie; gh-172
===

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
# legitimate waits.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi

# Test shim (dispatch_watch_test.dart): print the effective knobs and exit
# without dispatching anything.
if [ "${DW_DUMP_KNOBS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "budget=$budget queue_stall=$queue_stall poll=$poll cancel_wait=$cancel_wait"
  exit 0
fi

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING — fixed: the `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture is no longer inert, and the transient test now actually exercises the refresh**

Root cause confirmed exactly as reported: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so GNU/BSD `seq` exited 1 on every call, the swallowed failure left `body` empty, and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — the running-job count was always 0 regardless of the fixture.

**Stub fix** (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart, `stubGh`) — no `seq -f`, as suggested:

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
```

`n=0` → empty body → `{"jobs":[]}`; `n≥1` → comma-joined objects. The documented contract "absent file = 1 job always running" is now true (verified by a new test) instead of false.

**The stub now also logs every served count** to `served-jobs-<id>.log`, and the transient test asserts a running job was actually served before the gap — an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.

**Transient test rebuilt to exercise the refresh** (`a transient between-jobs pickup gap does not trip the guard`): it now runs with `DW_POLL_SECONDS=2` / `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3` — polls 1–2 report a running job (refresh), poll 3 reports the between-jobs gap only 2s old (inside the window), poll 4 completes. Both regressions from the finding now turn it RED:

- inert fixture (all polls serve 0): poll 3 trips the guard at 4s since start > 3s window → cancels the healthy child → exit 1 (reproduced in the RED run);
- `last_running="$now"` disabled (the exact experiment from the comment): the guard trips at poll 3 the same way → exit 1 (verified — the test previously stayed green with the refresh disabled, it now fails).

The queue-stall test additionally asserts the poll carries `--json status,conclusion,jobs` (see the merged-call thread) so the served count and status come from one snapshot.

Note: making the fixture honest exposed that the old `elif` chain also disarmed the **#34 budget** self-heal whenever a job was running (the budget was chained behind the refresh). The budget check now sits outside the refresh branch, pinned by a new test (`an absent jobs fixture = healthy running child: the #34 budget self-heal fires, never the stall guard`) — the original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held `in_progress` forever) only ever trips the budget.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT — fixed: the stall window now scales off the leg budget (`max(600, budget/8)`) and the residual class is documented**

Agreed — the fixed 600s could not distinguish a zombie-held pool from a legitimately busy one, and the "healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment was only true for the first (hosted) job of a chain. Taken option (b) **and** (c):

**scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh** — the default is no longer a constant:

```bash
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi
```

Effective windows: testflight 1875s (~31m), cli 2625s (~44m), play 825s (~14m), website/addin floored at 600s (~10m). The misleading comment is replaced with one that states the contention reality: the cli build-macos matrix serializes on fa-m5-1 and can hold the signature for hours; a testflight child legitimately shows nothing running all that time.

**Residual accepted class, documented in the script header and knob comment**: contention outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool). With the scaled windows the second-wedge arithmetic fits every leg ceiling — worst relative case addin: 2×(~10m version + 10m window) + 2×3m cancel ≈ 46m ≪ 150m; testflight ≈ 250m budget + 13m cancel + 31m stall ≈ 294m < 360m (daily-publish.yml comment updated; #351 budget/ceiling table untouched).

A new test pins the policy: `stall window defaults to max(600, budget/8) — scaled off the leg budget` asserts both the scaled branch (budget 8000s → window 1000s) and the floor (budget 800s → window 600s) via a `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim that prints the effective knobs without dispatching.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_2.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION — done: one `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call per poll**

The watch loop's two sequential calls are merged into a single snapshot call (the suggested shape, adjusted so both fields arrive on one line for a single `read`):

```bash
read -r status running < <(
  gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
    --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
) || true
if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
```

Both benefits landed: half the API traffic per poll in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and the between-call race (status says `in_progress`, the jobs call then reports 0 and ticks the stall clock for one iteration) is structurally impossible — status/conclusion and the running-job count now come from the same snapshot. API errors still degrade to `status="error/-"` + empty `running`, which counts as progress on both clocks.

The stub fixture in `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` was rebuilt to serve the merged shape (it pairs `view-<id>.txt` status lines with `jobs-<id>.txt` running-counts per poll), and the queue-stall test now asserts the merged `--json status,conclusion,jobs` invocation appears in the `gh` log.

{"content":"# gh-1722 rework — review threads addressed (3/3)

## Issues/Notes

- CI: no failed checks on the rework head (per `ci_failures.md`); no owned violations to fix.
- Three open review threads addressed: 1 BLOCKING (inert test stub fixture), 1 IMPORTANT (fixed 600s stall window false-wedges busy-pool children), 1 SUGGESTION (merge the two per-poll `gh run view` calls).
- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table and every `--budget-seconds`/`timeout-minutes` pair are untouched; only the stall **window** policy changed.

## Approach

**1. BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart)**

Confirmed: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so `seq` exited 1 on every call; the stub swallowed the failure and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — running-job count always 0, the "absent file = 1 job running" contract false, the refresh path untested.

- Stub body now built without `seq -f`:
  ```bash
  body=$(seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
  ```
  (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`, `n≥1` → comma-joined objects). The absent-file contract is now real and pinned by a test.
- The stub logs every served count to `served-jobs-<id>.log`; tests assert a running job was actually served, so an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.
- The transient-gap test was rebuilt to exercise the refresh with real timing (`DW_POLL_SECONDS=2`, `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3`): polls 1–2 report a running job, poll 3 reports a 2s-old gap (inside the window), poll 4 completes. Both regressions from the finding now turn it RED — verified in the RED run (inert fixture → healthy child cancelled) and by re-running the reviewer's own experiment (refresh line disabled → test fails; it previously stayed green).
- Making the fixture honest exposed a second defect the old `elif` chain hid: the **#34 budget** self-heal was chained behind the stall-clock refresh, so a run with a job `in_progress` (the original #34 zombie signature) could never trip the budget. The budget check now sits outside the refresh branch, pinned by a new test (`an absent jobs fixture = healthy running child: the #34 budget self-heal fires, never the stall guard`).

**2. IMPORTANT — fixed 600s stall window vs legitimately busy pools (scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh)**

The window now scales off the leg budget (options b+c from the thread):

```bash
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi
```

- Effective windows: testflight ~31m, cli ~44m, play ~14m, website/addin 600s floor.
- The misleading "a healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the contention reality (cli's build-macos matrix serializes on fa-m5-1 and can hold the "nothing running" signature for hours), and the residual accepted class (contention outliving the window but not the budget) is documented in the script header.
- Second-wedge arithmetic still fits every leg ceiling: worst relative case addin ≈ 46m ≪ 150m; testflight ≈ 250m + 13m cancel + 31m stall ≈ 294m < 360m (daily-publish.yml comment updated).
- Pinned by a new test asserting both the scaled branch (budget 8000s → 1000s) and the floor (budget 800s → 600s) via a `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim.

**3. SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` call per poll (scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh)**

The two sequential calls are merged into one snapshot call:

```bash
read -r status running < <(
  gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
    --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
) || true
if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
```

Half the API traffic per poll, and the between-call race (a run completing between the two calls ticks the stall clock for one iteration) is structurally impossible. API errors still degrade to progress on both clocks. The stub serves the merged shape (status/conclusion + jobs from paired fixtures per poll), and the queue-stall test asserts the merged invocation appears in the `gh` log.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — merged single-call polling; budget check decoupled from the stall-clock refresh; `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` default scaled to `max(600, budget/8)`; `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim; header/knob comments rewritten.

blocks.text:
epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # ONE gh call per poll (gh-172 review): status/conclusion and the
    # in_progress job count come from the same snapshot — half the API
    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.
    status=""
    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
    ) || true
    if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the gh-172 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    # The #34 budget check sits OUTSIDE the refresh branch below: the
    # original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held in_progress forever) shows
    # running>0 on every poll and only ever trips the budget — chaining the
    # budget behind the refresh would disarm it exactly when a job is
    # (nominally) running.
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$((now - last_running))" -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$wedge" ] && [ "$((now - started))" -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way, and
# the child is cancelled on the fail path so an orphaned queued run can
# never publish unattended when the pool revives. gh-172 review: the
# window is NOT a fixed 600s — it defaults to max(600, budget/8) because
# a healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the shared
# single-runner pool shows the same "nothing running" signature for hours
# (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on the one fa-m5-1 runner).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172 no-running-job wedge window, scaled off the
# leg budget so a busy shared pool is not mistaken for a zombie; gh-172
===

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
# legitimate waits.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi

# Test shim (dispatch_watch_test.dart): print the effective knobs and exit
# without dispatching anything.
if [ "${DW_DUMP_KNOBS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "budget=$budget queue_stall=$queue_stall poll=$poll cancel_wait=$cancel_wait"
  exit 0
fi

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING — fixed: the `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture is no longer inert, and the transient test now actually exercises the refresh**

Root cause confirmed exactly as reported: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so GNU/BSD `seq` exited 1 on every call, the swallowed failure left `body` empty, and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — the running-job count was always 0 regardless of the fixture.

**Stub fix** (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart, `stubGh`) — no `seq -f`, as suggested:

```bash
body=\$(seq "\$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
```

`n=0` → empty body → `{"jobs":[]}`; `n≥1` → comma-joined objects. The documented contract "absent file = 1 job always running" is now true (verified by a new test) instead of false.

**The stub now also logs every served count** to `served-jobs-<id>.log`, and the transient test asserts a running job was actually served before the gap — an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.

**Transient test rebuilt to exercise the refresh** (`a transient between-jobs pickup gap does not trip the guard`): it now runs with `DW_POLL_SECONDS=2` / `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3` — polls 1–2 report a running job (refresh), poll 3 reports the between-jobs gap only 2s old (inside the window), poll 4 completes. Both regressions from the finding now turn it RED:

- inert fixture (all polls serve 0): poll 3 trips the guard at 4s since start > 3s window → cancels the healthy child → exit 1 (reproduced in the RED run);
- `last_running="$now"` disabled (the exact experiment from the comment): the guard trips at poll 3 the same way → exit 1 (verified — the test previously stayed green with the refresh disabled, it now fails).

The queue-stall test additionally asserts the poll carries `--json status,conclusion,jobs` (see the merged-call thread) so the served count and status come from one snapshot.

Note: making the fixture honest exposed that the old `elif` chain also disarmed the **#34 budget** self-heal whenever a job was running (the budget was chained behind the refresh). The budget check now sits outside the refresh branch, pinned by a new test (`an absent jobs fixture = healthy running child: the #34 budget self-heal fires, never the stall guard`) — the original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held `in_progress` forever) only ever trips the budget.

{"content":"# gh-1722 rework — review threads addressed (3/3)

## Issues/Notes

- CI: no failed checks on the rework head (per `ci_failures.md`); no owned violations to fix.
- Three open review threads addressed: 1 BLOCKING (inert test stub fixture), 1 IMPORTANT (fixed 600s stall window false-wedges busy-pool children), 1 SUGGESTION (merge the two per-poll `gh run view` calls).
- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table and every `--budget-seconds`/`timeout-minutes` pair are untouched; only the stall **window** policy changed.

## Approach

**1. BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart)**

Confirmed: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so `seq` exited 1 on every call; the stub swallowed the failure and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — running-job count always 0, the "absent file = 1 job running" contract false, the refresh path untested.

- Stub body now built without `seq -f`:
  ```bash
  body=$(seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
  ```
  (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`, `n≥1` → comma-joined objects). The absent-file contract is now real and pinned by a test.
- The stub logs every served count to `served-jobs-<id>.log`; tests assert a running job was actually served, so an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.
- The transient-gap test was rebuilt to exercise the refresh with real timing (`DW_POLL_SECONDS=2`, `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3`): polls 1–2 report a running job, poll 3 reports a 2s-old gap (inside the window), poll 4 completes. Both regressions from the finding now turn it RED — verified in the RED run (inert fixture → healthy child cancelled) and by re-running the reviewer's own experiment (refresh line disabled → test fails; it previously stayed green).
- Making the fixture honest exposed a second defect the old `elif` chain hid: the **#34 budget** self-heal was chained behind the stall-clock refresh, so a run with a job `in_progress` (the original #34 zombie signature) could never trip the budget. The budget check now sits outside the refresh branch, pinned by a new test (`an absent jobs fixture = healthy running child: the #34 budget self-heal fires, never the stall guard`).

**2. IMPORTANT — fixed 600s stall window vs legitimately busy pools (scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh)**

The window now scales off the leg budget (options b+c from the thread):

```bash
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi
```

- Effective windows: testflight ~31m, cli ~44m, play ~14m, website/addin 600s floor.
- The misleading "a healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the contention reality (cli's build-macos matrix serializes on fa-m5-1 and can hold the "nothing running" signature for hours), and the residual accepted class (contention outliving the window but not the budget) is documented in the script header.
- Second-wedge arithmetic still fits every leg ceiling: worst relative case addin ≈ 46m ≪ 150m; testflight ≈ 250m + 13m cancel + 31m stall ≈ 294m < 360m (daily-publish.yml comment updated).
- Pinned by a new test asserting both the scaled branch (budget 8000s → 1000s) and the floor (budget 800s → 600s) via a `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim.

**3. SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` call per poll (scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh)**

The two sequential calls are merged into one snapshot call:

```bash
read -r status running < <(
  gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
    --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
) || true
if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
```

Half the API traffic per poll, and the between-call race (a run completing between the two calls ticks the stall clock for one iteration) is structurally impossible. API errors still degrade to progress on both clocks. The stub serves the merged shape (status/conclusion + jobs from paired fixtures per poll), and the queue-stall test asserts the merged invocation appears in the `gh` log.

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — merged single-call polling; budget check decoupled from the stall-clock refresh; `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` default scaled to `max(600, budget/8)`; `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim; header/knob comments rewritten.

blocks.text:
epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # ONE gh call per poll (gh-172 review): status/conclusion and the
    # in_progress job count come from the same snapshot — half the API
    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.
    status=""
    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
    ) || true
    if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the gh-172 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    # The #34 budget check sits OUTSIDE the refresh branch below: the
    # original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held in_progress forever) shows
    # running>0 on every poll and only ever trips the budget — chaining the
    # budget behind the refresh would disarm it exactly when a job is
    # (nominally) running.
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$((now - last_running))" -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$wedge" ] && [ "$((now - started))" -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool

# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way, and
# the child is cancelled on the fail path so an orphaned queued run can
# never publish unattended when the pool revives. gh-172 review: the
# window is NOT a fixed 600s — it defaults to max(600, budget/8) because
# a healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the shared
# single-runner pool shows the same "nothing running" signature for hours
# (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on the one fa-m5-1 runner).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172 no-running-job wedge window, scaled off the
# leg budget so a busy shared pool is not mistaken for a zombie; gh-172
===

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
# legitimate waits.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi

# Test shim (dispatch_watch_test.dart): print the effective knobs and exit
# without dispatching anything.
if [ "${DW_DUMP_KNOBS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "budget=$budget queue_stall=$queue_stall poll=$poll cancel_wait=$cancel_wait"

epoch=$(date +%s)
  if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
    echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
  if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

  started=$(date +%s)
  last_running="$started"
  while :; do
    # ONE gh call per poll (gh-172 review): status/conclusion and the
    # in_progress job count come from the same snapshot — half the API
    # traffic in a loop that polls every 60s for hours, and no
    # between-call race where a run completing between the two calls
    # ticks the stall clock for one iteration.
    status=""
    running=""
    read -r status running < <(
      gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
        --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
    ) || true
    if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    now=$(date +%s)
    # gh-172 job-level liveness: a run that is not completed but has NO job
    # in_progress is not making progress, however alive its status claims to
    # be — the gh-172 zombie-worker class holds the run in_progress AND the
    # single-runner pool forever, so the budget below alone would burn the
    # whole leg on a child that can never proceed. API errors count as
    # progress (never cancel a possibly-healthy run on a polling blip).
    # The #34 budget check sits OUTSIDE the refresh branch below: the
    # original #34 zombie (a SUCCEEDED job held in_progress forever) shows
    # running>0 on every poll and only ever trips the budget — chaining the
    # budget behind the refresh would disarm it exactly when a job is
    # (nominally) running.
    wedge=""
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      last_running="$now"
    elif [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$((now - last_running))" -gt "$queue_stall" ]; then
      wedge="no running job for ${queue_stall}s (gh-172 pool-held zombie signature)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$wedge" ] && [ "$((now - started))" -gt "$budget" ]; then
      wedge="still unfinished after ${budget}s"
    fi
    if [ -n "$wedge" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        # Containment (gh-172): cancel the child before failing so a
        # server-side-dead run can never start/publish unattended when the
        # pool revives — the 2026-10-20 re-dispatch sat queued for hours
        # after its leg was killed at the ceiling.
        gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
          || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id $wedge on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id $wedge — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

# (≈2x historical duration) is CANCELLED and re-dispatched exactly once;
# if the retry also wedges we fail fast naming both runs, so the pool
# problem surfaces in the leg log instead of silently eating 5 hours.
# gh-172 refines the wedge detection: budget expiry alone misses the
# pool-held zombie (run alive, nothing running) — a not-completed run with
# no in_progress job for DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS wedges the same way, and
# the child is cancelled on the fail path so an orphaned queued run can
# never publish unattended when the pool revives. gh-172 review: the
# window is NOT a fixed 600s — it defaults to max(600, budget/8) because
# a healthy child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the shared
# single-runner pool shows the same "nothing running" signature for hours
# (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on the one fa-m5-1 runner).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--budget-seconds N] \
#     [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the watch), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS (180), DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS (default
# max(600, budget/8) — gh-172 no-running-job wedge window, scaled off the
# leg budget so a busy shared pool is not mistaken for a zombie; gh-172
===

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
cancel_wait="${DW_CANCEL_WAIT_SECONDS:-180}"
# gh-172: how long a not-completed run may sit with NO job in_progress
# (everything queued or already done) before it is treated as a wedge.
# gh-172 review: a FIXED window cannot tell a zombie-held pool from a
# legitimately busy one — the same "nothing in_progress" signature is
# produced by a HEALTHY child queued behind a sibling leg's job on the
# shared single-runner pool (the cli build-macos matrix serializes on
# fa-m5-1 and can hold it for hours; a testflight child legitimately
# shows nothing running all that time). The default therefore scales off
# the leg budget: max(600, budget/8). Accepted residual class: contention
# outliving the window but not the budget still self-heals (cancel + one
# re-dispatch into a possibly-busy pool) — the second-wedge arithmetic
# (2×(~10m version + window) + cancel wait) fits every leg ceiling with
# the scaled windows, and the budget itself remains the backstop for long
# legitimate waits.
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi

# Test shim (dispatch_watch_test.dart): print the effective knobs and exit
# without dispatching anything.
if [ "${DW_DUMP_KNOBS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
  echo "budget=$budget queue_stall=$queue_stall poll=$poll cancel_wait=$cancel_wait"
  exit 0
fi

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION — done: one `gh run view --json status,conclusion,jobs` call per poll**

The watch loop's two sequential calls are merged into a single snapshot call (the suggested shape, adjusted so both fields arrive on one line for a single `read`):

```bash
read -r status running < <(
  gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \

{"content":"# gh-1722 rework — review threads addressed (3/3)

## Issues/Notes

- CI: no failed checks on the rework head (per `ci_failures.md`); no owned violations to fix.
- Three open review threads addressed: 1 BLOCKING (inert test stub fixture), 1 IMPORTANT (fixed 600s stall window false-wedges busy-pool children), 1 SUGGESTION (merge the two per-poll `gh run view` calls).
- No leg budget/ceiling arithmetic changed — the #351 table and every `--budget-seconds`/`timeout-minutes` pair are untouched; only the stall **window** policy changed.

## Approach

**1. BLOCKING — inert `jobs-<id>.txt` stub fixture (test/dispatch_watch_test.dart)**

Confirmed: `seq -f '{"status":"in_progress"}'` has no `%` directive, so `seq` exited 1 on every call; the stub swallowed the failure and every `--json jobs` poll answered `{"jobs":[]}` — running-job count always 0, the "absent file = 1 job running" contract false, the refresh path untested.

- Stub body now built without `seq -f`:
  ```bash
  body=$(seq "$n" | sed 's/.*/{"status":"in_progress"}/' | paste -sd, -)
  ```
  (`n=0` → `{"jobs":[]}`, `n≥1` → comma-joined objects). The absent-file contract is now real and pinned by a test.
- The stub logs every served count to `served-jobs-<id>.log`; tests assert a running job was actually served, so an inert stub can never fake the scenario again.
- The transient-gap test was rebuilt to exercise the refresh with real timing (`DW_POLL_SECONDS=2`, `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS=3`): polls 1–2 report a running job, poll 3 reports a 2s-old gap (inside the window), poll 4 completes. Both regressions from the finding now turn it RED — verified in the RED run (inert fixture → healthy child cancelled) and by re-running the reviewer's own experiment (refresh line disabled → test fails; it previously stayed green).
- Making the fixture honest exposed a second defect the old `elif` chain hid: the **#34 budget** self-heal was chained behind the stall-clock refresh, so a run with a job `in_progress` (the original #34 zombie signature) could never trip the budget. The budget check now sits outside the refresh branch, pinned by a new test (`an absent jobs fixture = healthy running child: the #34 budget self-heal fires, never the stall guard`).

**2. IMPORTANT — fixed 600s stall window vs legitimately busy pools (scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh)**

The window now scales off the leg budget (options b+c from the thread):

```bash
queue_stall="${DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS:-}"
if [ -z "$queue_stall" ]; then
  queue_stall=$((budget / 8))
  if [ "$queue_stall" -lt 600 ]; then queue_stall=600; fi
fi
```

- Effective windows: testflight ~31m, cli ~44m, play ~14m, website/addin 600s floor.
- The misleading "a healthy child assigns and starts its first job in seconds" comment is replaced with the contention reality (cli's build-macos matrix serializes on fa-m5-1 and can hold the "nothing running" signature for hours), and the residual accepted class (contention outliving the window but not the budget) is documented in the script header.
- Second-wedge arithmetic still fits every leg ceiling: worst relative case addin ≈ 46m ≪ 150m; testflight ≈ 250m + 13m cancel + 31m stall ≈ 294m < 360m (daily-publish.yml comment updated).
- Pinned by a new test asserting both the scaled branch (budget 8000s → 1000s) and the floor (budget 800s → 600s) via a `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim.

**3. SUGGESTION — one `gh run view` call per poll (scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh)**

The two sequential calls are merged into one snapshot call:

```bash
read -r status running < <(
  gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
    --jq '"\(.status)/\(.conclusion // "-") \([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length)"' 2>/dev/null
) || true
if [ -z "$status" ]; then status="error/-"; fi
```

Half the API traffic per poll, and the between-call race (a run completing between the two calls ticks the stall clock for one iteration) is structurally impossible. API errors still degrade to progress on both clocks. The stub serves the merged shape (status/conclusion + jobs from paired fixtures per poll), and the queue-stall test asserts the merged invocation appears in the `gh` log.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — merged single-call polling; budget check decoupled from the stall-clock refresh; `DW_QUEUE_STALL_SECONDS` default scaled to `max(600, budget/8)`; `DW_DUMP_KNOBS` test shim; header/knob comments rewritten.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — stub body construction fixed (`seq | sed | paste`), merged-shape serving, `served-jobs-<id>.log` fixture-honesty log; transient-gap test rebuilt with real timing; two new tests (absent-fixture/budget-while-running, scaled default window); merged-call assertion in the queue-stall test.
- `.github/workflows/daily-publish.yml` — gh-172 arithmetic comment updated for the scaled window (testflight ≈ 250m + 13m + 31m ≈ 294m < 360m); no behavioral change.

## Test Coverage

- TDD: all four touched/red tests failed against the pre-fix watcher (RED run reproduced: inert fixture cancels the healthy transient child; stall guard fires on a running child; no scaled default; no merged call), then went GREEN after the fix; the reviewer's vacuity experiment (`last_running="$now"` disabled) now fails the transient test instead of passing.
- `dart test test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 23 passed, 0 failed (correlation #343, wedge self-heal #344, gh-172 queue-stall group, workflow structural lint).
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see the result appended below.
- `dart analyze test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — clean; `bash -n scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — clean; `dart format` clean on the touched Dart file.

Full-suite result: **11383 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed**.
